evidence.quote: A conditioning image (e.g., H&E or DAPI) is processed by a ControlNet image encoder to extract spatial and morphological features.
It achieves this by creating a trainable copy of the diffusion model's encoder blocks (typically within the U-Net backbone) while keeping the original weights frozen.

biological_encoders.name: ControlNet image encoder / trainable ControlNet branch

evidence.quote: At each step, a cross-attention mechanism dynamically merges the morphological features from ControlNet with the semantic features from the text encoder.
These features are passed through 'zero convolution' layers (1x1 convolutions initialized with zeros) and added to the feature maps of the frozen denoising U-Net.

coverage_notes: The paper does not name the transformer-based text encoder or report its size, training state, vocabulary extension, or connector training state. It reports no controlled input-representation comparison, biological-input removal or corruption test, or synthetic text generator.

evidence.quote: We used two categories of metrics: 1) Clustering Similarity: To determine the similarity of two clusterings, we calculated the Fowlkes-Mallows Index (FMI) 18 . 2) Cell Type Classification Accuracy: We computed accuracy, precision, recall, and the F1-Score.

evidence.quote: Across 112 genes in the test data set, TissueCraftAI achieved a median F1 score of 0.24 compared to a 0.15 by Pix2Pix-Turbo (p = 0.0002).
This accuracy is further demonstrated by a high Kernel Density Estimate (KDE) similarity of 0.50.

evidence.quote: At the same time, a transformer-based text encoder processes the natural language query to generate a set of semantic feature vectors that capture the nuanced biological meaning of the specified molecular target.

The output was a parallel directory of "synthesized protein maps" where each input H&E patch was associated with multiple grayscale images. These images represented the predicted spatial expression of individual protein markers.

A key innovation of our approach is the use of natural language prompts, which allows users to flexibly query for any desired molecular target (e.g., "predict CD8 protein expression") without altering the model architecture.

representation_rationale.summary: Natural-language prompts support flexible querying of arbitrary molecular targets.

evidence.quote: Another limitation of existing methods is the lack of querying ability using natural language input for intuitive molecular target specification. Instead, existing methods require users to work with rigid, pre-defined marker outputs or gene name sentences 8,9 .

representation_rationale.summary: The authors criticize fixed marker outputs and gene-name sentence interfaces as rigid alternatives.

evidence.quote: To ensure the generated maps are spatially faithful to the input histology, our model is conditioned on the input image using a ControlNet module 13,14 , preserving the underlying tissue structure.

representation_rationale.summary: Conditioning on the histology image is intended to preserve spatial and tissue structure.
